'''Murat Abenovich Aitkhozhin''' ({{langx|kk|Murat Ábenuly Aıthojın}}, {{langx|ru|Мурaт Абенович Айтхoжин}}) (29 June 1939 – 19 December 1987) was a [[Kazakhstan|Kazakh]] [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] molecular biologist: the founder of [[molecular biology]] in [[Kazakhstan]]. He was the President of the [[Kazakhstan Academy of Sciences]] (1986–87), Deputy of [[Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union|The Supreme Soviet of the USSR]], member (and Chairman of the Kazakh branch) of the [[Soviet Peace Committee|Soviet Peace Fund]]. He was the founder and first Director of the Kazakh Institute of Molecular Biology and Biochemistry as well as being an Academician of the [[Kazakhstan Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences of the Kazakh SSR]] (1983), Doctor of Sciences (1977), Professor (1980) and [[Lenin Prize]] laureate (1976).

== Biography ==

=== Early career ===
Murat Aitkhozhin was born on 29 June 1939 in [[Petropavl]]ovsk in the [[Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic|Kazakh SSR]] in a large family. He was educated at the [[Al-Farabi Kazakh National University|Kazakh State University (KazGU)]] (graduated in 1962) and [[Moscow State University]] (graduated in 1965).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://mysl.kazgazeta.kz/?p=4803|title=ПАССИОНАРИЙ КАЗАХСТАНСКОЙ НАУКИ {{!}} Мысль - Республиканский общественно-политический журнал|last=admin|language=en-US|access-date=2020-01-04}}</ref>

In 1966, Aitkhozhin defended his thesis on “Ribonucleic Acids in the Early Embryogenesis of Loach Misgurnus fossilis” and between 1965 and 1967 he worked as a junior researcher. From 1967 to 1969 he was a senior research fellow at the Institute of Botany of the [[Kazakhstan Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences of the Kazakh SSR]], and became head of the laboratory in 1969.<ref>{{Cite book|chapter=Alma-Ata|last=Salmon|first=Gregory|title=Oxford Music Online|date=2002|publisher=Oxford University Press|doi = 10.1093/gmo/9781561592630.article.o007647|isbn=9781561592630}}</ref>

In 1976, he defended a doctoral dissertation at [[Moscow State University]] on the topic: "Ribonucleoprotein particles of higher plants." He was awarded the diploma No. 1 of a doctor of sciences in the specialty of [[molecular biology]]. In the same year he was awarded the most important prize of the USSR, the [[Lenin Prize]] for the discovery of a special class of [[ribonucleoprotein particle]]s, informosomes.<ref name=":0" />

=== Institute Director ===
In 1978, he became the director of the Institute of Botany of the [[Kazakhstan Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences of the Kazakh SSR]], and was elected as a Corresponding Member of the [[Kazakhstan Academy of Sciences|Academy]] the following year (1979).

In 1983, he founded the Institute of Molecular Biology and Biochemistry of the [[Kazakhstan Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences of the Kazakh SSR]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://imbb.org.kz/en/2019/05/21/murat-abenovich-ajthozhin/|title=Murat Abenovich Ajthozhin/|website=Институт молекулярной биологии и биохимии им. М. А. Айтхожин» КН МОН РК|language=en-US|access-date=2020-01-04}}</ref> and was elected to the position of Academician of the [[Kazakhstan Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences of the Kazakh SSR]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hanson|first=Gary|date=March 1992|title=A biographical directory of 100 leading Soviet officials|journal=Government Publications Review|volume=19|issue=2|pages=220–221|doi=10.1016/0277-9390(92)90101-g|issn=0277-9390}}</ref> The international recognition of the successes of [[molecular biology]] in Kazakhstan was the holding in 1984 of the international symposium "Prospects for bioorganic chemistry and molecular biology" at the institute. The symposium was attended by leading scientists in the field of molecular biology and bioorganic chemistry, dozens of [[Nobel Prize]] winners – including [[Linus Pauling]] and [[Dorothy Hodgkin]]. At this international symposium Aitkhozhin made a large plenary report.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

=== President of the Academy of Sciences ===
On 22 April 1986, at a turning point for the country and the republic, Aitkhozhin was elected as President of the [[Kazakhstan Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences of the Kazakh SSR]], a post in which he served until his death in 1987.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Мурат Айтхожин: он мало прожил, но очень много сделал |url=http://imbb.org.kz/2019/04/04/murat-ajthozhin-on-malo-prozhil-no-ochen-mnogo-sdelal/ |access-date=2020-01-04 |website=Институт молекулярной биологии и биохимии им. М. А. Айтхожин» КН МОН РК |language=ru-RU}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite book |title=Murat Aĭtkhozhin |others=Mutanov, G. (Galimkair), Мутанов, Г. (Галимкаир), Ăl-Farabi atyndaghy Qazaq ūlttyq universitetī, Әл-Фараби атындағы Қазақ ұлттық университеті |year=2015 |isbn=978-601-04-1167-8 |location=Almaty |oclc=962370306}}</ref>

On June 5, 1986, a session of the General Meeting of the Academy of Sciences of the Kazakh SSR was held, which was opened by the President of the Academy of Sciences of the Kazakh SSR, Academician M. A. Aitkhozhin, with the report "Tasks of scientists of the Academy of Sciences of the Kazakh SSR on the implementation of decisions of the [[27th Congress of the CPSU|XXVII Congress of the CPSU]] and XVI Congress of the [[Communist Party of Kazakhstan (Soviet Union)|Communist Party of Kazakhstan]]." At the session, [[Dinmukhamed Kunaev]], First Secretary of the [[Communist Party of Kazakhstan (Soviet Union)|Communist Party of Kazakhstan]] and member of the [[Politburo of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union|Politburo of the USSR]] also spoke.<ref>{{Cite book |url=http://nblib.library.kz/elib/Sait/NauBibUKAZ/%D0%9D%D0%B0%D1%83%D0%BA%D0%B0/%D0%A5%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B0%20%D0%90%D0%9D%20%D0%A0%D0%9A-PDF/Akademiya.pdf |isbn=978-601-203-002-0 |script-title=ru:Академия наук Республики Казахстан : хроника событий |lang=ru}}</ref>

Murat Aitkhozhin conducted tremendous organizational work as President of the Academy of Sciences of the Kazakh SSR – over the period under his leadership, the coordination of [[Scientific method|scientific research]] in Kazakhstan significantly improved and cooperation with leading [[Research institute|research centers]] was expanded, which ensured the passage of academic science to the modern frontiers of scientific and technological progress.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://nblib.library.kz/elib/library.kz/jurnal/v_2009_3/MuratAbenovish0903.pdf|title=MuratAbenovish0903|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220420000408/http://nblib.library.kz/elib/library.kz/jurnal/v_2009_3/MuratAbenovish0903.pdf|archive-date=2022-04-20}}</ref>

As president of the Academy of Sciences, Aitkhozhin paid great attention to the training of young scientific personnel. Being a professor at [[Al-Farabi Kazakh National University|Kazakh State University]], he taught a self-developed course in [[molecular biology]] and special courses on [[biochemistry]] for many years. He created the only dissertation council in the [[Central Asia|Central Asian region]] on the defense of [[Candidate of Sciences|candidate dissertations]] in molecular biology and biochemistry. Additional funds were allocated to expand the list of leading journals from abroad according to the profiles of sciences obtained by the Central Scientific Library of the Academy of Sciences.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Он верил в созидательную силу фундаментальной науки {{!}} Номад {{!}} 27.06.2014 |url=https://nomad.su/?a=15-201406270014 |access-date=2020-05-13 |website=nomad.su}}</ref>

== Contribution to Science ==
Murat Aitkhozhin was the founder of [[molecular biology]] and [[biotechnology]] in Kazakhstan. Aitkhozhin was engaged in the search and study of the physicochemical properties of informosomes in plant cells in the group of academician [[Alexander Spirin|A.S. Spirin]]. The group discovered classes of plant informosomes - free cytoplasmic, polysomal-linked, and nuclear, including RNA-binding proteins. For this work, they were awarded the [[Lenin Prize]] in 1976.<ref name=":2">{{Cite book|title=Severo-Kazachstanskaja oblast' ėnciklopedija|date=2005|publisher=Izdat. Arys|others=Bajmen, Ch., Nordkasachstan|isbn=9965-17-306-0|location=Almaty|oclc=931533772}}</ref>

In 1983, Aitkhozhin founded the Institute of Molecular Biology and Biochemistry of the [[Kazakhstan Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences of the Kazakh SSR]]. In 1987, he organized the Kazakh Agricultural Biotechnology Center, where work is carried out on cell and genetic engineering of plants. Murat Aitkhozhin first introduced the course of molecular biology and a number of special courses for students of the biological faculty of the [[Al-Farabi Kazakh National University|Kazakh State University]].<ref name=":2" />

Under the leadership of Aitkhozhin, a set of instruments for the automation of molecular biological experiments was developed, which was protected by 15 copyright certificates and 16 patents in leading countries.<ref name=":2" />

== Contribution to Public life ==
Along with science, Murat Aitkhozhin also took part in the party life of the country. Murat Aitkhozhin was elected a deputy of the [[Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union|Supreme Soviet of the USSR]] of the 11th convocation ([[Soviet of the Union]]) from the Chapaevsky constituency of the [[Ural (region)|Ural region]]<ref name=":3" /> and a delegate to the [[27th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union|XXVII Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union]].<ref name=":3" />

Murat Aitkhozhin was a member of the [[Soviet Peace Committee|Soviet Peace Fund]], and was appointed Chairman of the [[Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic|Republican]] branch of the Soviet Peace Fund in 1981. Furthermore, he was appointed to the Presidium of the [[Kazakhstan Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences of the Kazakh SSR]] (in 1981). Along with future [[President of Kazakhstan]], [[Nursultan Nazarbayev]], Aitkhozhin was in the Kazakh delegation to Latvia in 1977.<ref name=":3" /> He was awarded the Gold Medal of the [[Soviet Peace Committee|Soviet Peace Fund]] in 1987 as well as the [[Order of Friendship of Peoples|Order of the Friendship of Peoples]].<ref name=":3" />

He was one of the signatories of the article “We Are Bitter” in the newspaper “Evening Alma-Ata” dated 12/27/1986 in which he condemned the actions of the [[Jeltoqsan|Jheltoqsans]], quote “..What right were these hooligans, most of whom were under the influence of alcohol and drugs ..."<ref name=":4">{{Cite news|url=https://rus.azattyq.org/a/bibigul_tulegenova_kazakh_singer/24176362.html|title=Казахские звёзды на службе у авторитарной власти|website=Радио Азаттык|date=28 June 2012 |language=ru|access-date=2020-01-04 |last1=Токаева |first1=Асем }}</ref> However, his colleague, M. K. Gilmanov believes that Aitkhozhin was forced to sign this article, perhaps due to his membership in the Kazakh national-patriotic organisation "Zhas Tulpar" in his youth, and his support of the Kazakh language in science.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Оралқызы |first=Айымгүл |date=2017-06-30 |title=Әлем таныған академикті қазақ танымайды… {{!}} 30.06.17 |url=https://massaget.kz/persona/alem-tanyigan-akademikt-kazak-tanyimaydyi--46791/ |access-date=2026-11-12 |website=Massaget.kz |language=kk}}</ref>

Murat Aitkhozhin was in 1983–1987 a member of the [[Lenin Komsomol Prize]] Award Committee in the field of science and technology and in 1986-1987 he was chairman of the Committee on [[State Prizes of the Soviet Republics|State Prizes]] in Science and Technology under the [[Government of Kazakhstan|Council of Ministers of the Kazakh SSR]]. He was chairman of the scientific council on physical and chemical biology at the Presidium of the Academy of Sciences of the Kazakh SSR, member of the editorial Board of the Union journals “Molecular biology”, “Biopolymers and cell”, was the editor-in-chief of the journal “Bulletin of the Kazakh SSR”.<ref name=":1" />

== Awards ==
Source:<ref name=":4" />
* [[Jubilee Medal "In Commemoration of the 100th Anniversary of the Birth of Vladimir Ilyich Lenin"|Jubilee Medal "For Valiant labour - In Commemoration of the 100th Anniversary of the Birth of Vladimir Ilyich Lenin"]] (1970).
* Is entered in the Golden Book of Honour of the [[Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic|Kazakh SSR]] (1974).

* Gold Medal of the [[Soviet Peace Committee|Soviet Peace Fund]] (1987).
* [[Order of Friendship of Peoples|Order of the Friendship of Peoples]] (1987).

== Legacy ==
Named after Academician Murat Aitkhozhin:

* Secondary school number 1 in [[Petropavl]]ovsk.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://b141.sko.agartu.kz/|title=Главная - №1 орта мектеп. Средняя школа № 1|last=Consulting|first=BenchMark|website=Главная - №1 орта мектеп. Средняя школа № 1|access-date=2020-01-04}}</ref>
* Institute of Molecular Biology and Biochemistry of the [[Kazakhstan Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences of Kazakhstan]].
* 2 scholarships for graduate students of the [[Kazakhstan Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences of Kazakhstan]] in the field of biology.
* Prize for young scientists of the [[Kazakhstan Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences of Kazakhstan]] in the field of biological sciences.
* A commemorative plaque adorns the building of the house where Murat Aitkhozhin lived.
* On the occasion of the 60th anniversary of Murat Aitkhozhin, a memorial museum was created at the Institute of Molecular Biology and Biochemistry to commemorate his life and works.<ref name=":3" />

In 2016, Murat Aitkhozhin was chosen as one of the nominees in the "Science" category of the national project «El Tulgasy» (Name of the Motherland) The idea of the project was to select the most significant and famous citizens of [[Kazakhstan]] whose names are now associated with the achievements of the country. More than 350,000 people voted in this project, and Aitkhozhin was voted into 5th place in his category.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ЕЛ ТҰЛҒАСЫ / ИМЯ РОДИНЫ / События / Разделы сайта / Деловой журнал Exclusive|url=http://exclusive.kz/el-tulgasy-2016/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170321153157/http://exclusive.kz/el-tulgasy-2016/|url-status=dead|archive-date=2017-03-21|date=2017-03-21|access-date=2020-05-13}}</ref>
